To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neutrino oscillations are observable if the neutrino production coherence condition is satisfied, and that the oscillation probabilities averaged over the neutrino source and detector are the same as those obtained by coherent summation of amplitudes, provided that the neutrino production and detection processes are coherent and that the parent particle is considered as point like.

neutrino oscillations are observable if the neutrino production process is localized on a scale smaller than the oscillation length and the neutrino production and detection processes are localized in the same point in space.

neutrino oscillations in the standard three neutrino framework are observable only if all three coherence conditions are satisfied: (1) neutrino production coherence; (2) oscillation coherence; (3) detection coherence.
